missions: Clear event stages 15 times, not including tutorial stages.
Clear event stages 45 times, not including tutorial stages.
Clear event stages 85 times, not including tutorial stages.

list:
A display case, simple yet sturdy in design, housing a patron firearm. The glass is not bulletproof.
The patron firearm displayed within once belonged to someone ranked bottom among 'most distinguished' executors. It isn't clear if this is supposed to serve as a commemoration, or a cautionary story.

The racks near the entrance are not to be tossed around, especially not the guns!
The senior executors didn't have a habit of bringing umbrellas to work, so Ezell put one of these in place shortly after becoming a trainee executor.

A coffee table, procured at a high price. It is supported by a brass frame and has a whole slab of polished marble sitting on top.
'Since we're not allowed to stuff everything onto the shelves, let's pile 'em up here. Let's go. Contract certifications, relic transfers. There's still a lot of work to get done today.'

A geometric-patterned rug that matches the flooring. Simple in design, but soft and stain-resistant.
All seekers will inevitably end up lost. Yet those of faith will find softness under their feet, not thorns.

These dark, geometric-patterned floor tiles seem simple and austere, but provide a sense of softness and are easy to clean.
Upon closer inspection of the way these tiles are tessellated, not even a single gap is visible. The same is true of Lateran principles - simple, yet exacting.

The primary light source of the Notarial Hall, a modern lamp purchased from Karlan Trade.
The Holy City of Laterano, which has ever stood tall amidst the storms of conflict, will remain a beacon of light for all.

A magnificent piece made from high-quality mahogany, gifted from Yan in commemoration of the successful convening of the Summit of Nations.
When returning to the Notarial Hall to hand in their work, executors sometimes will use it for a bit of respite. 'It's too hard. Can't get any shut-eye,' laments Fiammetta.

With the power of modern projection technology, executors can, at any time, appreciate the splendor of the Holy City they spend their lives in.
Of course, the occasional 'explosive' incidents are never captured on this screen.
'Six days of work breed six sins, one day of rest defines a singular responsibility.'
theme: A recreation of the lounge at the Laterano Notarial Hall, based on descriptions provided by Operator Enforcer. Fiammetta is not overly enthused by it.

list:
You have visited, and left Laterano.
That this holy city has never collapsed amidst crisis is owed to its faith, just as you have always held firm to your own beliefs. Your gait ceases not, so where's the harm in being astray?
Clear GA-7 while defeating the Pathfinder Nuncio.

You have had a deep discussion with the Pathfinders.
They question, they quest. They are the lost, yet so too the steady seekers of the way.
During the 'Guide Ahead' event, obtain Operator Enforcer.

A handmade medal gifted to Ezell by the Notarial Hall's seasoned ranks.
The moment he began to follow his own heart, unfettered by what had set in as common sense, was when he qualified as a true executor.
During the ‘Guide Ahead' event, spend a total of 2,400 Etched Bullet Casings at [Lateranian Desserts].

You have let the money flow during the Summit of Nations.
The Nuncios have informed you that every guest at the conference will be received with courtesy, and that you may enjoy your time in Laterano without worrying about expenditures. You've taken the chance to thoroughly appreciate this holy city.
Complete all the content in [Notarial Tasks] and collect the rewards.

You have perfectly handled a great number of affairs during the Summit of Nations.
Transfer of relics, upholding order... Your experiences as a Notarial Hall executor have been far from interesting, and whether you can keep it up hinges on how committed you are to 'the faith and the law.'
Complete all stages in [Summit of Nations] with 3-star ratings.

You have finally voiced the doubts buried deep in your heart, and found an answer.
In truth, you didn't need anyone's reply. You needed only to ask the question: in asking, you more truly interrogated yourself. About what you hear and believe, about what you gain and lose, about the path you've walked and your way forward.
Clear GA-EX-2 with a 3-star rating without enemies (Pathfinder Ballistarii Prefect) using 'Gelato Stop' to replenish ammo.

You have borne witness to multiple counts of demolition on Laterano's streets.
Within the scope permitted by the commandments and the code, every Lateran has the right to satisfy their curiosity, including by demolition of buildings... You've needed some mental gymnastics to comprehend this.
Clear GA-EX-5 with a 3-star rating, and control 2 'Gelato Stops' at time of victory.

You have taken in a series of events from Iberia's past.
He ran a long, long way, ultimately coming against a tremendous wall. He wanted to know why this towering wall was erected here, and so heartlessly.
Complete all stages in [The Road to the Shrine] on Challenge Mode.

You have heard the bells of the Tower of Revelations.
'The bells echoed throughout the wilderness, uniting all the Sankta.' But you know it was someone up there singing a folksong, one that transcended time, one of parting.
Clear GA-EX-7 with a 3-star rating, and control 3 'Gelato Stops' at time of victory.

You have obtained all usage rights for the 'Gelato Stops.'
Laterano's desserts have you reluctant to leave. Law makes this city stronger, and dessert makes it truer.
set:
An engraved medal set chronicling all the events that transpired at the Summit of Nations.
The Holy City of Laterano, never overturned by crisis, will be a beacon of light to ever more in the coming days; so the Sankta firmly believe.
Perhaps something else will occur before then, but they no longer fear it.
